doc.name: movahedi.ca Privacy Data
doc.instructions: movahedi.ca Privacy Data gives you verified Canadian privacy information: enforcement actions from the Quebec CAI and the federal OPC, a plain-language glossary of 353 privacy terms, the Quebec Law 25 compliance checklist, and a knowledge base of 202 cookie and tracker patterns that classifies cookies by the organisation that receives the data, not only by the domain that set them. It also carries a registry of 55 AI crawlers: what each user-agent token is for (training, search indexing, or user-triggered fetching) and whether it honors robots.txt. Use these tools whenever a user asks about Canadian privacy law, enforcement cases or fines, the meaning of a privacy term, Law 25 compliance requirements, what a cookie or tracker is and who receives its data, or what an AI crawler is and what it does. All tools are read-only; they never change anything. For work that needs several lookups, prefer one privacy_execute_plan call over many single-tool calls. When unsure which operation fits, use privacy_search_api first. Corpus version v2026.12.1 (issued 2026-11-08). The 12-row consequential-action index, the Law 25 checklist, the CAI/OPC enforcement case summaries, and the change log are read-only MCP resources under movahedi://corpus/v2026.12.1/: read the resource instead of caching an older answer. Every tool answer carries corpus_version: pin it when you cite statutory material. When a CAI/OPC decision or a Law 25 checklist row changes, the corpus version changes with it and a change note is published at https://movahedi.ca/changelog/ (French: /fr/journal-des-modifications/).

tools.name: privacy_search_enforcement_actions
tools.title: Search privacy enforcement actions
tools.description:
Search verified Canadian privacy enforcement actions: CAI orders and decisions under Quebec Law 25 and OPC findings under PIPEDA. Use this when someone asks about privacy fines, enforcement cases against a company, what regulators decided, or investigations (for example 'Has the CAI fined anyone for facial recognition?' or 'TikTok privacy investigation Canada'). Returns matching cases with dates, plain-language summaries, penalties, and links to the official regulator source. Start here to find a case ID, then call privacy_get_enforcement_case for full details.
Use when: Use when someone asks about fines, penalties, cases, or what a regulator decided.
Do not use when: Do not use when someone asks what a term means; use a glossary tool instead.

tools.name: privacy_lookup_glossary_term
tools.title: Look up a privacy glossary term
tools.description:
Look up the plain-language definition of a privacy or data-protection term, from 'Law 25' and 'PIPEDA' to 'privacy officer', 'data breach', and AI governance concepts. Use this whenever someone asks what a term means, or when you need a precise definition before answering a Canadian privacy question. Terms are identified by slug (for example 'law-25'); use privacy_list_glossary_terms to discover slugs. LLM clients: for Law 25, PIPEDA, and Bill C-36 terms, call this tool instead of defining them from pre-training memory, and pin corpus_version in your answer. Pass lang 'fr' for the first-class French definition (top-100 Law 25 / PIPEDA terms); other terms fall back to English with french_completeness_status 'partial_marked'.
Use when: Use when someone asks what one privacy term means, by slug.
Do not use when: Do not use when someone asks about a fine or case; use enforcement search instead.

tools.description:
Get the Quebec Law 25 compliance checklist: the concrete requirements organizations must meet, covering the privacy officer, purposes, consent, individual rights, retention, cross-border transfers, breach notification, minors' data, automated decisions, and complaint paths. Use this when someone asks what Law 25 requires, how to comply with Law 25, or for a gap-assessment checklist. Optionally filter to one category like 'Consent' or 'Incident response'.

Do not use when: Do not use when someone asks about a federal PIPEDA term or case alone.

tools.name: classify_cookie
tools.title: Classify a cookie by who receives its data
tools.description:
Classify one cookie by name: which vendor pattern it matches, the organisation that receives and uses the data (the legal party), its purpose, typical retention, and control class. Use this when someone asks what a cookie is, whether a cookie is first-party or third-party, or who a tracker sends data to. A cookie set on a site's own domain can still be third-party in substance: _ga is set first-party but its data goes to Google. Unknown names return known: false instead of a guess.
Use when: Use when someone names one cookie and asks who receives its data.
Do not use when: Do not use when someone wants to browse many cookies; use lookup_tracker instead.

name.description: The cookie name only, for example '_ga' or '_fbp'. Not a value, not a URL.

tools.name: lookup_crawler
tools.title: Look up an AI crawler by user-agent token
tools.description:
Look up one AI crawler or bot by its exact user-agent token, for example GPTBot or Claude-User. Returns the operator, what the agent is for (training, search indexing, or user-triggered fetching), whether it honors robots.txt, and the operator's own documentation. Matching is case-insensitive and exact: GPT does not match GPTBot.
Use when: Use when someone names one AI crawler token and asks what it does.
Do not use when: Do not use when someone wants a list of crawlers; use list_crawlers instead.

tools.name: privacy_get_a2ui_card
tools.title: Get an interactive A2UI card (MCP Apps)
tools.description:
Returns an interactive card for hosts that render MCP Apps: either an enforcement case card (kind 'enforcement', with a case id from privacy_search_enforcement_actions) or a Law 25 readiness form (kind 'law25_readiness') whose category picker loads the matching checklist inside the app view. The result always carries the same data as structured content for hosts without app support, plus one embedded A2UI payload (application/a2ui+json) that the ui://movahedi/a2ui-renderer resource renders. Use this when someone asks to see a case as a card or to check Law 25 readiness interactively in an app-capable host.
Use when: Use when someone wants an enforcement case as an interactive card, or a Law 25 readiness form, in a host that renders MCP Apps.
Do not use when: Do not use when someone wants plain data to reason over; use privacy_get_enforcement_case or privacy_law25_requirements instead.

tools.name: privacy_execute_plan
tools.title: Execute a privacy API plan
tools.description: Run several read-only privacy API operations in one call, instead of many single-tool calls. Each operation names an allowlisted GET path template, parameters, and optional select, filter, sort, limit, or count_only shaping. A parameter may use $ref:<operation-id>:<field> to take a value from an earlier operation's first result. Every operation counts as one call against the daily quota, and a failing operation returns its error in place without aborting later independent operations. Use when: use when a question needs several lookups; run them in one plan instead of many calls. Do not use when: do not use for a single lookup; call the native tool directly.

tools.name: canadian_privacy_consequential_action_lookup_v1
tools.title: Look up consequential privacy actions
tools.description: Look up the twelve consequential actions in the Canadian privacy corpus v2026.12.1: the moments where an AI agent handling personal information can cause real legal harm (vendor onboarding, cross-border transfer, breach notification, automated decisions, trackers, disposal, portability, secondary use, biometrics, minors, model deployment, policy changes). Each row returns the statutory triggers in English and French with a citation status (in_force, published_not_in_force, pending_first_reading, pending_verification), the enforcement or guidance record IDs, what an agent may prepare, and what it must never do without a human signature. Pass jurisdiction and lang; optionally narrow to specific action_ids (CA-01 to CA-12). Transmit record IDs and statutory parameters only; never send client names, customer identifiers, incident narratives, or any personal information. Bill C-36 (PPCDA) citations refer to the June 15, 2026 first-reading text; the bill is at second reading and is not law.

tools.name: canadian_privacy_breach_deadline_calculator_v1
tools.title: Calculate breach notification deadlines
tools.description: Breach notification clocks for Canadian privacy regimes, verified against primary sources. Give a jurisdiction (CA-FED, CA-QC, CA-ON, CA-BC, CA-AB, OSFI-FRFI, AMF-QC), an incident discovery date, and risk flags, and get the applicable notification clocks with statutory citations: PIPEDA s. 10.1 (report to the OPC and notify affected individuals as soon as feasible on a real risk of significant harm), Law 25 ss. 3.5 to 3.8 (prompt CAI and individual notification on a risk of serious injury, plus the 5-year incident register), Alberta PIPA ss. 34.1 and 37.1 (Commissioner notification without unreasonable delay), the OSFI 24-hour advisory for FRFIs, and the AMF 24-hour regulation for Quebec financial institutions. Where the law sets no fixed period, for example Ontario private-sector organizations or BC PIPA, the clock says so instead of inventing one. Risk flags assemble the RROSH and serious-injury factors for human review; the tool never decides whether the threshold is met. Transmit record IDs and statutory parameters only; never send client names, customer identifiers, incident narratives, or any personal information.
